outlets.name: Time
outlets.summary: Time is leading with the Trump administration's threat to demolish the Kennedy Center and an apparent Iranian threat against Barron Trump, alongside the South Carolina primary result and Canada's tariff retaliation.

items.headline: Trump administration warns the Kennedy Center could be demolished
items.detail: The Justice Department argues the memorial faces a financial and structural death spiral without Trump's help.

items.headline: What to know about the apparent Iranian threat against Barron Trump
items.detail: Time examines the reported threat against the president's son as the Iran conflict continues.

items.headline: Darline Graham Nordone wins the South Carolina GOP Senate primary runoff
items.detail: The Trump-backed candidate won the runoff to contest the seat of her late brother, Lindsey Graham.

items.headline: Canada retaliates against Trump's tariffs with levies of up to 50%
items.detail: Ottawa announced retaliatory tariffs on US goods as the trade war between the two countries escalates.

items.headline: Two people have died of measles in Pennsylvania
items.detail: The deaths come amid a measles outbreak in the state, according to Time.

outlets.name: Variety
outlets.summary: Variety is dominated by the death of Dolly Parton and the ongoing Paramount-Warner Bros merger fight, including Iowa's Supreme Court push and Jane Fonda's clash with the studio, plus Meta's $17.1 billion settlement.

items.headline: Dolly Parton, queen of country music, dies at 80
items.detail: The singer, songwriter and actress died Tuesday in Nashville at 80.

items.headline: Meta to pay $17.1 billion in a settlement with 29 states over social-media addiction
items.detail: The deal resolves claims brought by state attorneys general over the platforms' alleged harm to young users.

items.headline: Iowa's attorney general says she is taking California to the Supreme Court over the Paramount-Warner Bros lawsuit
items.detail: Brenna Bird wrote she is suing California for leading the charge in the antitrust challenge to the merger.

items.headline: Jane Fonda slams Paramount for calling Mark Ruffalo's comments antisemitic
items.detail: The actress called the studio's response a smear to delegitimise criticism of the merger.

items.headline: 'Heroes' stars throw a reunion to celebrate the life of Hayden Panettiere
items.detail: The cast gathered to honour the late actress, sharing so much love, gratitude and warmth.

outlets.name: Bloomberg
outlets.summary: Bloomberg is leading on the ECB's hawkish signal on rates, the slide in oil as Iran and Oman push to reopen Hormuz, and copper's record run, with the Bessent bond-market play in focus.
outlets.note: Homepage fetch timed out; items sourced from the Bloomberg markets RSS feed and dated article URLs.

items.headline: ECB's Schnabel says rates must rise more on a resilient economy
items.detail: European Central Bank Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said interest rates must rise further as the Middle East conflict keeps pressure on the economy.

items.headline: Oil extends declines as Iran and Oman push talks to reopen Hormuz
items.detail: Crude fell for a third day as the two countries discussed a potential deal to resume shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Copper climbs from a record-high close with supply still tight
items.detail: Copper steadied after earlier gains took it closer to a record high, with short-term supplies continuing to look tight.

items.headline: The 'Bessent Put' might actually be working for the bond market
items.detail: A week after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent jolted markets with his plan to bring down US borrowing costs, the impact is becoming clearer.

outlets.name: BBC
outlets.summary: The BBC is leading with the deadly flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border and the death of Dolly Parton, alongside the Pakistan hospital fire, Prince Harry and Meghan's return to the UK, and the escalating US-Canada trade war.

items.headline: Hundreds missing and 31 dead as a flash flood hits the Nepal-Tibet border
items.detail: The missing include more than 100 people from India and 12 from the UK, with CCTV capturing a wall of mud and water hitting a border crossing.

items.headline: The door was locked at the Pakistan hospital where a fire killed 14 babies
items.detail: Witnesses said the door to the ward was locked, though a hospital official told the BBC it was manned with security guards to protect the babies.

items.headline: Prince Harry and Meghan land in the UK days after announcing their move
items.detail: The couple and their two children are believed to have flown into the country privately from California.

items.headline: Dolly Parton dies from cancer aged 80 as the world remembers her
items.detail: The legendary country music singer died surrounded by loved ones, her representatives said.

items.headline: Canada's retaliation tests the limit of American power under Trump
items.detail: The president is using US dominance to challenge allies and enemies alike, but both Canada and Iran have found ways to fight back.

outlets.name: France 24
outlets.summary: France 24 is leading with the Nepal-Tibet flash flood disaster and the Middle East live coverage of the Iran conflict, alongside the CIA chief's Moscow visit and El Nino-fuelled drought emergencies in the Americas.
outlets.note: Items taken from the dated live-news wire index, all with 20260826 URL stamps.

items.headline: At least 22 bodies recovered and hundreds missing after Nepal-Tibet flash floods
items.detail: Chinese state media reported the mudslide disaster resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port on the Tibetan side of the border.

items.headline: Netanyahu says a diplomatic deal is not possible with Iranian 'savages'
items.detail: The Middle East live blog tracks the latest as Iran says the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite transit-corridor talks with Oman.

items.headline: Kremlin says the CIA chief met Russian counterparts, not Putin, in Moscow
items.detail: Russia confirmed CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Russian intelligence services during a visit to the capital.

items.headline: Panama and El Salvador declare an emergency over El Nino-fuelled drought
items.detail: Both countries declared emergencies as a powerful El Nino drives severe drought conditions across the region.

items.headline: Trump sends the Saudi civil nuclear agreement to Congress for review
items.detail: The classified pact is aimed at bolstering Riyadh's nuclear programme but remains contingent on Saudi Arabia normalising relations with Israel.

outlets.name: Al Jazeera
outlets.summary: Al Jazeera is leading with the Iran war's economic toll, including the rial's collapse and the Hormuz route talks with Oman, alongside the Nepal flash flood and the Pakistan hospital fire.

items.headline: Iran says it received new military equipment as Hormuz remains closed
items.detail: Tehran said damaged infrastructure has been repaired even as the Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite a route deal with Oman.

items.headline: At least 22 killed and hundreds missing after a Nepal flash flood
items.detail: An avalanche of ice and rock triggered massive flash floods that swept through parts of Nepal, killing at least 22 people.

items.headline: Iran and Oman agree on a temporary Hormuz route
items.detail: The two countries reached an agreement on a temporary shipping route through the strategic strait, according to Al Jazeera.

items.headline: At least 14 babies killed in a Pakistan hospital nursery fire
items.detail: A fire swept through a hospital nursery in Pakistan, killing at least 14 newborn babies.

items.headline: One US dollar now costs 2 million rials in Iran
items.detail: Sanctions and the US-Israel war on Iran have left the country's people unable to keep pace with rising prices.
